items.name: Remote login (SSH)
items.says: Keys only: passwords don't work. Someone with an account here can sign in over the network and run commands.
items.fix: sudo systemctl disable --now ssh.socket (if you reach this computer over SSH, that cuts you off)

items.name: File sharing (Samba)
items.says: Off. Other computers can open the folders this one shares.

items.name: File sharing (AFP)
items.says: Off. Older Macs can open the folders this one shares.

items.name: NFS file sharing
items.says: Off. Other computers can mount the folders in /etc/exports. NFS asks for no password: it trusts the address a computer says it has.

items.name: Screen sharing (VNC)
items.says: Off. Someone can see this screen and, with the password, use it.

items.name: Remote desktop (RDP)
items.says: Off. Someone with an account here can sign in to this desktop over the network.

items.name: Printer sharing (CUPS)
items.says: Off. Other computers can print on the printers this one shares.

items.name: FTP server
items.says: Off. Files and passwords cross the network unencrypted, so anyone on the way can read them.

items.name: Telnet
items.says: Off. Everything typed, passwords too, crosses the network unencrypted.

items.name: Cockpit web console
items.says: Off. Anyone with an account here can manage this server from a web browser.

items.name: Webmin
items.says: Off. Anyone with a Webmin login can manage this server from a web browser.

items.name: Media server
items.says: Off. Devices on the network can browse and play the music and videos it serves.

items.name: Port 80
items.says: Other computers can connect to nginx on port 80, usually a web server.
items.fix: Have nginx listen on 127.0.0.1 only, or switch it off: sudo systemctl disable --now nginx

items.name: Port 3000
items.says: Other computers can connect to python3 on port 3000, usually a web app.
items.fix: Have shop-dev listen on 127.0.0.1 only, or switch it off: sudo systemctl disable --now shop-dev

items.name: Port 3001
items.says: Other computers can connect to python3 on port 3001.
items.fix: Have python3 listen on 127.0.0.1 only, or stop it: bsweep ports stop 3001

items.name: alex
items.says: Can become the administrator; password locked; 2 SSH keys can log in; sudo asks no password: anyone who gets into this account controls the machine; last logged in 6 Nov.
items.fix: Remove NOPASSWD for alex with sudo visudo (and the files in /etc/sudoers.d)

items.name: root
items.says: Can become the administrator; password locked.

items.name: Firewall
items.says: Off: everything listed as open to the network can be reached by any computer that can reach this one.
items.fix: sudo ufw allow OpenSSH && sudo ufw enable (allow SSH first). A cloud firewall counts too
